<!-- pr-reviewer: f459981150522f876a4110b7b033cecde952cabb -->
**Ready for the maintainer to merge** (one thing to know about the stack, below).

## What looks good
- The #1230 change itself is wording only. `setup_align::generation_problem` keeps the same condition (`kind_of_setup(world, Some(&setup)) != Kind::Mill`) and now names the kind through the one `machine_kind_name` table. `kind_of_setup` already reads the setup's own machine (`setup_mount::own_machine`, document machine only as fallback), so there is no second derivation and no latent wrong-setup read.
- The message is plain English and names both the setup and the kind: "setup 'X' holds the part turned (part alignment) - an aligned part is not supported yet on a sinker EDM machine".
- Pinning test `an_aligned_setup_on_an_edm_names_the_edm_kind_it_is_refused_on` covers sinker and wire EDM, and asserts neither "lathe" nor "mill-turn" appears.
- No `unwrap`/`expect`/`panic!` added outside tests; no goldens, snapshots, CHANGELOG or process files touched; `Changelog:` and `Fixes #1230` present; decision note included.

## The stock-sim files (checked specifically)
Those changes (`stock_sim.rs`, `stock_sim_carry.rs`, `tests/carried_fixtures_cache.rs`) are not #1230's: they come from the stacked commit `12185329` (#1229 / #1182, carry refusal names the kind). #1230's own commit only moves the name `match` out of `carry_machine_refusal` into a shared `machine_kind_name` and re-exports it.
- Text only. The carry condition in `carry_turn` is unchanged (`one_machine` -> `kind(m_to.1) != Mill`), and `one_machine` still compares both setups' `machine_of`, so the different-machines refusal is untouched. No carried-stock verdict, no lattice/engine path, no cache key or fixture reading changes; nothing was a wrong-machine read before, only a wrong word ("lathe or mill-turn" for a sinker/wire/plasma setup).
- `CARRY_MACHINE_REFUSAL` became a prefix ("...not supported yet on a") with the kind appended; every reader still goes through `carry_turn`, so all paths say the same thing.
- The `carried_fixtures_cache.rs` change is a tightening, not a loosening: the lathe/mill-turn test now also requires "on a lathe machine" / "on a mill-turn machine", and a new test pins the sinker carry refusal and that a mill still carries.

## Local results (PR head merged with current origin/main: clean, "Already up to date")
- `cargo test -p camcraft-app --lib`: 147 passed
- `setup_align` 10, `carried_fixtures_cache` 7, `stock_sim_document` 9, `setup_carry` 9, `rest_across_setups` 7, `carried_verify` 8 - all passed, 0 failed
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-app --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean

## Requested before merge
None.

## Notes (not blocking)
1. Stack: the PR says "stacked on #1229" but its base is `main`, and #1229 is still open (labelled `conflicts`). Merging this PR therefore lands #1229's carry-refusal change too, unreviewed under its own number. I read that diff above and it is sound, but the maintainer may prefer to merge #1229 first or accept that #1229 closes with this one (its `Fixes #1182` is not in this PR's body).
2. The new alignment test uses one machine for the whole document; the "two setups on different machines, each named by its own kind" case is not pinned for the alignment message. The accessor is per-setup so it should hold, but a test with Setup1 on a mill and Setup2 on a sinker would pin it.
3. The decision note says `setup_stock.rs` doc wording changed; it did (comment only).

A maintainer will approve and merge by hand.
